plan.root_cause: The modal's focus trap only returns focus after a focusin event, which fails to prevent focus from leaving when shift+tabbing from the first focusable element, allowing focus to escape to the opener button.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the modal element to intercept Tab and Shift+Tab keys and wrap focus within the modal's focusable elements, preventing default when at the boundaries.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Shift+Tab from the first focusable element (close button) will now move focus to the last focusable element (Delete button) within the modal, meeting the requirement.
functional_risks: May interfere with custom keyboard shortcuts that rely on Tab or Shift+Tab inside the modal.
If the modal contains no focusable elements, the listener will prevent tabbing entirely (though this is unlikely).
Could conflict with assistive technologies that expect default tabbing behavior to leave the modal via the opener (though escape remains available).
verification_requirements: After opening the modal, pressing Tab moves focus through close button, input field, cancel button, delete button and wraps back to close button.
Pressing Shift+Tab from the delete button moves focus to cancel button, input field, close button and wraps to delete button.
The Escape key continues to close the modal.
Clicking outside the modal or on the backdrop still returns focus to the modal when appropriate.
The modal's focus trap still works for mouse clicks and programmatic focus loss.

plan.root_cause: The modal's focus trap only returns focus after a focusin event, which fails to prevent focus from leaving when shift+tabbing from the first focusable element, allowing focus to escape to the modal element (tabindex=-1) instead of wrapping to the last focusable element (Delete button). The modal lacks a keydown listener to cycle focus within its focusable elements.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the modal element to intercept Tab and Shift+Tab keys and wrap focus within the modal's focusable elements, preventing default when at the boundaries. Initialize this listener when the modal is shown (with focus) and remove it when hidden.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Shift+Tab from the first focusable element (close button) will now move focus to the last focusable element (Delete button) within the modal, meeting the requirement. Tab from the last focusable element will wrap to the first.
functional_risks: May interfere with custom keyboard shortcuts that rely on Tab or Shift+Tab inside the modal.
If the modal contains no focusable elements, the listener will prevent tabbing entirely (though this is unlikely).
Could conflict with assistive technologies that expect default tabbing behavior to leave the modal via the opener (though escape remains available).
verification_requirements: After opening the modal, pressing Tab moves focus through close button, input field, cancel button, delete button and wraps back to close button.
Pressing Shift+Tab from the delete button moves focus to cancel button, input field, close button and wraps to delete button.
The Escape key continues to close the modal.
Clicking outside the modal or on the backdrop still returns focus to the modal when appropriate.
The modal's focus trap still works for mouse clicks and programmatic focus loss.
